**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)

**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 57
**Title (English, from literature):** Bathing too often

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 57, titled *Nahāna* ("Bathing too often"), is an expiation rule within the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka regulating monastic bathing habits. Under this rule, a monk residing in the central Ganges plain who bathes more than once a fortnight—except under prescribed exceptions such as being dirty or unwell—commits an offense that must be confessed. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali. None of the secondary literature passages in the dossier directly examine this text; rather, they refer to the distinct rule Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 57 or constitute unrelated non-Buddhist citations.

 It also lists corresponding rules for nuns, including Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 138.
